name: Perkin reaction
reagents: aromatic aldehyde; acid anhydride (e.g. acetic anhydride)
catalyst: alkali salt of the acid (e.g. NaOAc, K2CO3)
definition: An aldol condensation where an aryl aldehyde reacts with an acid anhydride to form a cinnamic acid.

name: Diels-Alder reaction
reagents: diene; dienophile (alkene/alkyne)
definition: A [4+2] cycloaddition reaction where a diene reacts with a compound containing a double or triple bond (a dienophile) to form an unsaturated six-membered ring compound.

name: Michael addition
reagents: Michael donor (enolate, malonate, nitroalkane); Michael acceptor (enone, acrylate)
definition: A conjugate addition reaction where a carbon nucleophile adds to the beta-carbon of an alpha,beta-unsaturated system (or an activated carbon-carbon bond).

name: Grignard reaction
reagents: Grignard reagent (RMgX); aldehyde/ketone/ester/nitrile; aqueous acid workup (NH4Cl, H3O+)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where a Grignard reagent reacts with a compound containing an electrophilic carbon atom. A Grignard reagent is a magnesium-stabilised carbon nucleophile. An aldehyde leads to a secondary alcohol, a ketone leads to a tertiary alcohol, an ester leads to a ketone and a nitrile leads to a ketone.

name: Wittig reaction
reagents: phosphonium salt; strong base (n-BuLi, NaH, KOtBu, NaHMDS); aldehyde/ketone
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where a carbonyl compound reacts with a phosphonium ylide to give an alkene.

name: Sandmeyer reaction
reagents: aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+, from NaNO2/HX); CuCl, CuBr or CuCN
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(I) halide or pseudohalide to form an aromatic halide or pseudohalide.

name: Gattermann halogenation
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with copper powder and hydrochloric acid or hydrobromic acid to form an aromatic chloride or bromide.

name: Koerner-Contardi reaction
reagents: aryl diazonium salt; copper(II) halide (CuCl2, CuBr2)
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(II) halide to form an aromatic halide.

name: Heck reaction
reagents: aryl/vinyl halide or triflate; alkene; base (Et3N, K2CO3)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where an organohalide or triflate couples to a terminal olefin to produce an internal olefin, catalysed by palladium. It is stereospecific.

name: Beckmann rearrangement
reagents: oxime; acid (H2SO4, PPA, TsCl, PCl5, SOCl2)
definition: A rearrangement where an oxime rearranges to form an amide. Often there is selective migration of one group.

name: Cope rearrangement
reagents: 1,5-diene
definition: A [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement where a 1,5-hexadiene rearranges to form a 1,5-hexadiene.

name: Baeyer-Villiger oxidation
reagents: ketone; peracid (mCPBA, peracetic acid, TFPAA) or H2O2 with Lewis acid
definition: A reaction of a ketone to give an ester, in which an alkyl, benzyl or phenyl group migrates from one of the alpha-carbon centres to an adjacent oxygen, displacing an oxygen-based leaving group; the result is a formal insertion of an oxygen atom. The reaction also works with aldehydes, giving the corresponding carboxylic acid. The term \"Baeyer-Villiger rearrangement\" may occasionally be used in a mechanistic sense to refer specificially to the actual rearrangement step.

name: Mannich reaction
reagents: non-enolisable aldehyde (typically formaldehyde); primary/secondary amine or NH3; enolisable carbonyl compound
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where ammonia or an amine reacts with a non-enolisable aldehyde, often methanal, and an enolisable carbonyl compound to form a beta-amino carbonyl compound.

name: Mitsunobu reaction
reagents: alcohol; triphenylphosphine (PPh3); DEAD or DIAD; acidic pronucleophile (carboxylic acid, phthalimide, HN3, phenol)
definition: A substitution where an alcohol is converted into something else. Typical reagents are a dialkyl azodicarboxylate and a triarylphosphine. The alcohol stereocentre is inverted.

name: Stille coupling
reagents: organostannane (R-SnBu3); organic halide or triflate
catalyst: Pd(PPh3)4 or Pd2(dba)3; CuI additive optional
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where a stannane reacts with an organohalide or organotriflate.

name: Reformatsky reaction
reagents: alpha-haloester; zinc metal; aldehyde or ketone
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where an aldehyde or amine reacts with a alpha-halo ester and zinc to form a beta-hydroxy ester.

name: Clemmensen reduction
reagents: ketone/aldehyde; zinc amalgam (Zn(Hg)); concentrated HCl
definition: A functional group reduction where an aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group is reduced to a methylene with zinc-mercury amalgam and hydrochloric acid.

name: Ullmann reaction
reagents: aryl halide (2 equiv.); copper powder
definition: A carbon-carbon homocoupling reaction of an aryl halide mediated by copper.

name: Birch reduction
reagents: arene; alkali metal (Na or Li); liquid NH3; alcohol (EtOH, tBuOH)
definition: Addition of hydrogen atoms to aromatic rings by means of alkali metals in liquid ammonia.

name: Claisen condensation
reagents: two ester molecules (with alpha-H); alkoxide base (NaOEt)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction of an ester and a carbonyl compound to form a beta-keto ester.

name: Knoevenagel condensation
reagents: aldehyde/ketone; active methylene compound (malonate, cyanoacetate); weak base (piperidine, pyridine)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction of an aldehyde and a methylene compound.

name: Friedel-Crafts acylation
reagents: arene; acyl chloride or anhydride; Lewis acid (AlCl3, FeCl3)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between an arene and a carbonyl compound (usually an acyl halide) to give an aryl ketone. The reaction is catalysed by a Lewis acid.

name: Friedel-Crafts alkylation
reagents: arene; alkyl halide; Lewis acid (AlCl3, FeCl3)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between an arene and an alkyl halide/alkene/alcohol (anything that can form a carbocation) to give a substituted arene. The reaction is catalysed by a Lewis acid.

name: Oppenauer oxidation
reagents: secondary alcohol; excess ketone (acetone); aluminium alkoxide (Al(OiPr)3)
definition: An oxidation of a secondary alcohol to a ketone involving an equilibrium between the alcohol and a reagent ketone present in excess, catalysed by a metal alkoxide.

name: Prins reaction
reagents: alkene; aldehyde (typically formaldehyde); acid catalyst (H2SO4, Lewis acid)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling between formaldehyde and an alkene to give a 1,3-diol or an allylic alcohol, catalysed by acid.

name: Wolff rearrangement
reagents: alpha-diazoketone
catalyst: Ag2O, light (hv) or heat; nucleophile (H2O, ROH, R2NH)
definition: A rearrangement of a diazoketone to give a ketene, with the elimination of molecular nitrogen.

name: Bischler-Napieralski reaction
reagents: beta-arylethylamide; dehydrating agent (POCl3, P2O5, Tf2O)
definition: A cyclodehydration of a beta-phenethylamide to give a 3,4-dihydroisoquinoline.

name: Curtius rearrangement
reagents: acyl azide (from acyl chloride + NaN3 or acid + DPPA); heat; nucleophile (H2O, ROH, amine)
definition: A rearrangement of an acyl azide to give an isocyanate by pyrolysis, with the elimination of molecular nitrogen.

name: Vilsmeier-Haack reaction
reagents: electron-rich arene; DMF (or N-methylformanilide); POCl3
definition: A formylation of an activated arene with a disubstituted formamide to give an arenecarbaldehyde.

name: Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons reaction
reagents: phosphonate ester; base (NaH, KOtBu, LiCl/DBU); aldehyde/ketone
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between a phosphonate and a carbonyl compound to give an olefin.

name: Horner reaction
reagents: phosphine oxide carbanion (R2P(O)CH2R'); strong base (n-BuLi); aldehyde/ketone
definition: A joining reaction between a phosphine oxide and a carbonyl compound to give an olefin.

name: Ritter reaction
reagents: nitrile; carbocation source (tertiary alcohol, alkene); strong acid (H2SO4)
definition: A reaction between an alcohol or alkene and a nitrile to give an amide, catalysed by a Bronsted acid.

name: Pictet-Spengler reaction
reagents: beta-arylethylamine (tryptamine); aldehyde or ketone
definition: A condensation-cyclisation of a beta-phenethylamine with an aldehyde to give a tetrahydroisoquinoline.

name: Arbuzov reaction
reagents: trialkyl phosphite (P(OR)3); alkyl halide
definition: The alkylation of a trialkyl phosphite with an alkyl halide or acyl halide to give an alkyl phosphonate.

name: Mukaiyama aldol condensation
reagents: silyl enol ether; aldehyde/ketone; Lewis acid (TiCl4, BF3·OEt2)
definition: An aldol condensation between an aldehyde or ketone and a silyl enol ether (also known as a ketene silyl acetal) to give a beta-hydroxy carbonyl compound.

name: Skraup reaction
reagents: aniline; glycerol; sulfuric acid; oxidant (nitrobenzene, As2O5); FeSO4 moderator
definition: A condensation between an aromatic amine and glycerol to give a quinoline.

name: Arndt-Eistert reaction
reagents: carboxylic acid chloride; diazomethane (CH2N2); Ag2O (or Ag benzoate); water/alcohol/amine
definition: A homologation reaction of a carboxylic acid to give the homologated carboxylic acid via acyl chloride and diazoketone intermediates.

name: Fischer indole synthesis
reagents: arylhydrazine; aldehyde or ketone; acid (ZnCl2, PPA, HCl, AcOH)
definition: Reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with a phenylhydrazine to give an indole.

name: Dieckmann cyclisation
reagents: diester; alkoxide base (NaOEt, KOtBu)
definition: An intramolecular cyclisation of a diester to give a cyclic beta-ketoester.

name: Staudinger reaction
reagents: azide; phosphine (PPh3); H2O (Staudinger reduction) or carbonyl (aza-Wittig)
definition: A joining of an organic azide and a tertiary phosphine to give a phosphazo compound.

name: Dimroth rearrangement
reagents: heterocycle (e.g. 1-alkyl-2-iminopyrimidine); base or aqueous acid
definition: A rearrangement of a heterocyclic compound in which endocyclic and exocyclic heteroatoms swap places.

name: Edman degradation
reagents: peptide N-terminus; phenyl isothiocyanate (PITC); anhydrous acid (TFA)
definition: A cleaving reaction in which a peptide is treated with phenylisothiocyanate, removing the terminal amino acid group, to form the chain-shortened amine and a phenylthiohydantoin.

name: Reimer-Tiemann reaction
reagents: phenol; chloroform (CHCl3); strong aqueous base (NaOH/KOH)
definition: A formylation reaction between a phenol and chloroform (for example, to form an ortho-formyl phenol).

name: Wurtz reaction
reagents: alkyl halide (2 equiv.); sodium metal
definition: A carbon-carbon homocoupling reaction of two molecules of an alkyl halide with sodium to give a symmetrical product.

name: Baylis-Hillman reaction
reagents: aldehyde; activated alkene (acrylate, MVK); tertiary amine catalyst
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling of an aldehyde to an activated alkene in the presence of a nucleophilic base to give an alpha-hydroxyalkylated compound.

name: Darzens reaction
reagents: ketone/aldehyde; alpha-haloester; base (NaOEt, KOtBu)
definition: A coupling of an aldehyde or ketone with an alpha-halo ester to form an alpha,beta-epoxy ester, which hydrolyses to yield aldehydes or ketones by elimination of carbon dioxide.

name: Boc protection
reagents: amine or alcohol; di-tert-butyl dicarbonate (Boc2O); base (Et3N, DMAP, NaOH)
definition: A protection reaction in which an amine is converted into a tert-butoxycarbonyl compound.

name: Peterson olefination
reagents: alpha-silyl carbanion (Me3SiCH2MgCl or Me3SiCH2Li); aldehyde/ketone; acid or base for elimination
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction in which an alpha-silyl carbanion reacts with an aldehyde or a ketone to give an alkene, proceeding via a beta-hydroxysilane. The stereochemistry of the alkene can be controlled by treating the intermediate with acid or base.

name: Ullmann condensation
reagents: aryl halide; alcohol, phenol, amine or thiol; copper; base (K2CO3, Cs2CO3)
definition: A coupling reaction in which a phenol is coupled to an aryl halide to give a diaryl ether in the presence of a copper compound.

name: Goldberg reaction
reagents: aryl halide; amide; copper; base
definition: A coupling reaction in which an acetanilide is coupled to an aryl halide to give an N-acetyl diaryl amine in the presence of a copper compound.

name: Paternò–Büchi reaction
reagents: carbonyl compound; alkene
definition: A photochemical cycloaddition between an aldehyde or ketone and an alkene to give an oxetane.

name: Barbier reaction
reagents: alkyl halide; magnesium/zinc/indium metal; carbonyl compound (in situ organometallic)
definition: A joining reaction between an aldehyde or ketone and an alkyl halide or aryl halide or vinyl halide or allyl halide in the presence of metal to give a secondary or tertiary alcohol.

name: Henry reaction
reagents: nitroalkane; aldehyde/ketone; base (NaOH, Et3N, KOtBu)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between a nitroalkane and an aldehyde or ketone to give a beta-hydroxy nitroalkane.

name: Barton reaction
reagents: alkyl nitrite (RONO); light
definition: The photolytic oxidation of a nitrate ester to give a gamma-nitroalcohol.

name: Negishi coupling
reagents: organozinc halide (RZnX); organic halide or triflate
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between an organohalide or organotriflate and an organozinc compound. The reaction is catalysed by palladium or nickel.

name: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction
reagents: ketone/aldehyde; isopropanol; aluminium isopropoxide (Al(OiPr)3)
definition: A reduction of an aldehyde or ketone to an alcohol involving an equilibrium between the aldehyde or ketone and a reagent alcohol present in excess, catalysed by a metal alkoxide. This reaction is the reverse of the Oppenauer oxidation (RXNO:0000047).

name: Williamson ether synthesis
reagents: alkoxide (alcohol + NaH/KOH/NaOH); alkyl halide (primary)
definition: The reaction between an alkyl halide or alkyl sulfate and a metal alkoxide to give an ether.

name: Wittig methylenation
reagents: phosphonium salt; strong base (n-BuLi, NaH, KOtBu, NaHMDS); aldehyde/ketone
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where a carbonyl compound reacts with a phosphonium ylide to give a terminal alkene.

name: Ramberg-Bäcklund reaction
reagents: alpha-halosulfone; base (KOH, KOtBu)
definition: The reaction of an alpha-halosulfone to give an alkene, with the extrusion of sulfur dioxide.

name: Fischer-Hepp rearrangement
reagents: N-nitrosoaniline; HCl
definition: The rearrangement of an aromatic nitrosamine to a para-nitrosoaniline.

name: Glaser coupling
reagents: terminal alkyne; base (NH3/amine); Cu(I) salt; oxidant (O2/air)
definition: A coupling reaction between two molecules of a terminal alkyne catalysed by Cu(I) salts.

name: Eglinton reaction
reagents: terminal alkyne; stoichiometric copper(II) acetate; pyridine
definition: A coupling reaction between two molecules of a terminal alkyne using stoichiometric Cu(II) salts.

name: Cadiot-Chodkiewicz coupling
reagents: terminal alkyne; 1-haloalkyne; amine base
definition: A coupling reaction between a terminal alkyne and an alkynyl halide catalysed by Cu(I) salts.

name: Leuckart reaction
reagents: aldehyde/ketone; ammonium formate or formamide
definition: The reductive amination of ketones or aldehydes with an ammonium formate or formamide to form an amine.

name: Leuckart-Wallach reaction
reagents: aldehyde/ketone; amine; formic acid
definition: The reductive amination of ketones or aldehydes with an amine and formic acid to form amines.

name: Gabriel synthesis
reagents: potassium phthalimide; primary alkyl halide; hydrazine or aqueous acid/base (deprotection)
definition: The reaction of primary alkyl halides with sodium or potassium phthalimide, followed by hydrolysis, to give the corresponding primary amine.

name: Ing-Manske procedure
reagents: potassium phthalimide; primary alkyl halide; hydrazine hydrate
definition: The reaction of primary alkyl halides with sodium or potassium phthalimide, followed by treatment with hydrazine, to give the corresponding primary amine.

name: Hunsdiecker reaction
reagents: silver carboxylate; bromine or iodine
definition: The decarboxylation of silver carboxylates with halogens to give organic halides.

name: Pfitzinger reaction
reagents: isatin; carbonyl compound with alpha-CH2; base (KOH)
definition: The reaction between isatin and an alpha-methylene carbonyl compound to give a substituted quinoline-4-carboxylic acid.

name: Grob fragmentation
reagents: 1,3-difunctional substrate (e.g. 3-halo-alcohol, 1,3-diol monotosylate); base (KOtBu, NaH)
definition: The fragmentation of a molecule that takes place when an electron-donating fragment (X) and an electron-accepting fragment (X') are situated at positions 1 and 3 on an aliphatic chain, to give a cationic fragment, a neutral fragment (e.g. an alkene) and an anionic fragment.

name: Brook rearrangement
reagents: alpha-/beta-/gamma-hydroxysilane; catalytic base
definition: The rearrangement of an alpha-, beta- or gamma-hydroxy silane to give a silyl ether. It is catalysed by a base.

name: Nicholas reaction
reagents: propargylic alcohol/ether; Co2(CO)8; Lewis acid (BF3·OEt2); nucleophile; oxidant (CAN) to release alkyne
definition: The reaction of a propargylic cation (stabilised with dicobalt octacarbonyl) with a nucleophile to give a substituted alkyne.

name: Nicholas reaction, nucleophilic heteroatom centre
reagents: propargylic alcohol/ether; Co2(CO)8; Lewis acid (BF3·OEt2); nucleophile; oxidant (CAN) to release alkyne
definition: The reaction of a propargylic cation (stabilised with dicobalt octacarbonyl) with a hydride or amine or enamine to give a substituted alkyne.

name: Nicholas reaction, nucleophilic carbon centre
reagents: propargylic alcohol/ether; Co2(CO)8; Lewis acid (BF3·OEt2); nucleophile; oxidant (CAN) to release alkyne
definition: The reaction of a propargylic cation (stabilised with dicobalt octacarbonyl) with a nucleophilic carbon centre (on e.g. enolates, allyl silanes, ketones, electron-rich aromatics, beta-dicarbonyl compounds) to give a substituted alkyne.

name: Julia olefination
reagents: alkyl phenyl sulfone; strong base (n-BuLi); aldehyde; acylating agent (Ac2O/BzCl); Na/Hg or SmI2
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between a phenyl sulfone and an aldehyde or ketone to give a (typically trans) alkene.

name: Sommelet reaction
reagents: benzylic halide; hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA); water/acid
definition: The oxidation of a benzylic halide to give an aldehyde. The reaction uses hexamethylenetetramine.

name: Bouveault-Blanc reaction
reagents: ester; sodium metal; absolute ethanol
definition: The reduction of an ester using sodium to give two alcohols.

name: Payne rearrangement
reagents: 2,3-epoxy alcohol; aqueous NaOH (base)
definition: A base-catalysed isomerisation of a 2,3-epoxyalcohol, with inversion of configuration at C2.

name: Baker-Venkataraman rearrangement
reagents: o-acyloxyacetophenone; base (KOH, KOtBu, NaH)
definition: The base-catalysed rearrangement of an o-acetoxyacetophenone to give a hydroxyphenyl-1,3-diketone.

name: Bamford-Stevens reaction
reagents: tosylhydrazone; strong base (NaOMe, NaH) in protic solvent
definition: The reaction of a tosylhydrazone of an aldehyde or ketone with a strong base to give an olefin.

name: Shapiro reaction
reagents: tosylhydrazone; alkyllithium (2 equiv., e.g. n-BuLi, MeLi); electrophile or H2O
definition: The reaction of a tosylhydrazone of an aldehyde or ketone with an alkyllithium or Grignard reagent to give an olefin.

name: Doebner reaction
reagents: aromatic aldehyde; malonic acid; pyridine (with piperidine)
definition: The reaction between an aromatic amine, an aldehyde and pyruvic acid on heating to give a quinoline 4-carboxylic acid (cinchoninic acid).

name: Balz-Schiemann reaction
reagents: aryl amine; HBF4; NaNO2 (diazonium tetrafluoroborate); heat
definition: The conversion of an aromatic amine to the corresponding fluoride via the diazonium fluoroborate.

name: Kolbe electrolysis
reagents: carboxylate salt; electric current (electrolysis)
definition: The decarboxylation and coupling of a carboxylate or mixture of carboxylates to give a dimer.

name: Ugi reaction
reagents: aldehyde; amine; carboxylic acid; isocyanide
definition: Reaction of a ketone or aldehyde, amine, an isocyanide and carboxylic acid to form a bisamide.

name: Wacker-Tsuji oxidation
reagents: terminal alkene; PdCl2; CuCl (or Cu(OAc)2); O2; water
definition: The oxidation of a terminal alkene or ethene to a methyl ketone or acetaldehyde, catalysed by PdCl2 and CuCl2, and using molecular oxygen as the oxidant.

name: Wacker process
reagents: ethylene; O2; PdCl2; CuCl2; water
definition: The oxidation of ethene to acetaldehyde, catalysed by PdCl2 and CuCl2, and using molecular oxygen as the oxidant.

name: Monsanto process
reagents: methanol; carbon monoxide (CO); HI/MeI
definition: The reaction of carbon monoxide with methanol to form acetic acid, catalysed by a rhodium complex.

name: Cativa process
reagents: methanol; carbon monoxide; HI/MeI
definition: The reaction of carbon monoxide with methanol to form acetic acid, catalysed by an iridium complex.

name: Barton-McCombie deoxygenation
reagents: alcohol; base (NaH); CS2; MeI (xanthate formation); Bu3SnH; AIBN
definition: The deoxygenation of an alcohol to the corresponding alkane using a thiochloroformate. It proceeds by a radical mechanism.

name: Barton decarboxylation
reagents: carboxylic acid; N-hydroxy-2-thiopyridone/thiohydroxamate ester; Bu3SnH; AIBN or light
definition: The decarboxylation of a carboxylic acid to the lower homologue alkane using a pyridine thione.

name: Rosenmund reduction
reagents: acyl chloride; H2; Pd/BaSO4; poisoned catalyst (quinoline-S)
definition: The hydrogenolysis of an acyl halide to the corresponding aldehyde, catalysed by palladium-on-barium sulfate.

name: Sonogashira coupling
reagents: aryl/vinyl halide or triflate; terminal alkyne; amine base (Et3N, iPr2NH)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where a terminal alkyne reacts with an aryl halide to give an aryl alkyne. It is catalysed by palladium.

name: Gattermann reaction
reagents: arene; HCN and HCl (or Zn(CN)2/HCl); AlCl3
definition: The formylation of an arene with hydrogen cyanide to give an aryl aldehyde or ketone.

name: Suzuki-Miyaura coupling
reagents: organoboron (boronic acid/ester); organic halide or triflate; base (K2CO3, Cs2CO3, K3PO4)
definition: The coupling of a boronic acid or boronic ester with an unsaturated halide, triflate or sulfonate catalysed by a palladium(0) complex.

name: Sharpless asymmetric epoxidation
reagents: allylic alcohol; Ti(OiPr)4; diethyl tartrate (DET); tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP)
definition: The epoxidation of an allylic alcohol to give a beta,gamma-epoxy alcohol, with control of absolute stereochemistry at the two new stereocentres. The oxidising agent is tert-butyl hydroperoxide, and the catalyst is a complex of titanium salt and optically active diethyl tartrate.

name: Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation
reagents: alkene; OsO4 (cat.) or K2OsO2(OH)4; chiral ligand ((DHQ)2PHAL/(DHQD)2PHAL); K3Fe(CN)6 or NMO; K2CO3 (AD-mix)
definition: The dihydroxylation of an alkene to give an alpha,beta-diol, with control of absolute stereochemistry at the two new stereocentres. The oxidising agent is osmium tetroxide, which is used catalytically with a stoichiometric oxidant and a chiral ligand. The reagents are available commercially as AD-mix.

name: Sharpless asymmetric aminohydroxylation
reagents: alkene; nitrogen source (chloramine-T, TsNClNa, or carbamate + tBuOCl); OsO4 (cat.); chiral ligand ((DHQ)2PHAL)
definition: The aminohydroxylation of an alkene to give a beta-amino alcohol, with control of absolute stereochemistry at the two new stereocentres. The oxidising agent is an oxygen-containing osmium species and/or an amino derivative which can be used catalytically with a stoichiometric oxidant and a chiral ligand.

name: Kumada coupling
reagents: Grignard reagent; organic halide; Ni or Pd catalyst
definition: A cross-coupling reaction between a Grignard reagent and an activated (aryl or vinyl) halide or triflate. The reaction is catalysed by a palladium or nickel catalyst.

name: Barbier-Wieland degradation
reagents: methyl ketone/ester; aryl Grignard; dehydration (Ac2O or acid); oxidation (CrO3) to shorten chain
definition: The degradation of a carboxylic acid to its next lower homologous carboxylic acid.

name: Corey-Fuchs reaction
reagents: aldehyde; CBr4; PPh3; n-BuLi (2 equiv.)
definition: A homologation reaction of an aldehyde to yield a terminal alkyne. The reagents are tetrabromomethane, triphenylphosphine, butyllithium and water.

name: Emde degradation
reagents: quaternary ammonium salt; Na/Hg or Zn/H+
definition: A reduction of a quaternary ammonium salt containing at least one unsaturated substituent, to give a tertiary amine.

name: Claisen rearrangement
reagents: allyl vinyl ether
definition: The [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of an allyl vinyl ether to give a gamma,delta-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

name: Ireland-Claisen rearrangement
reagents: allyl ester; strong base (LDA); chlorotrimethylsilane (TMSCl)
definition: The enolisation and subsequent [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of an allylic acetate to give a gamma,delta-unsaturated carboxylic acid.

name: Bellus-Claisen rearrangement
reagents: allylic amine/ether; acyl halide (with tertiary base)
definition: The coupling and subsequent [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of an allylic ether or allylic thioether or allylic amine and a ketene to give the corresponding gamma,delta-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

name: Eschenmoser-Claisen rearrangement
reagents: allylic alcohol; N,N-dimethylacetamide dimethyl acetal; heat
definition: The coupling and subsequent [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of an allylic alcohol and alpha,alpha-dialkoxy ethylamine to give a gamma,delta-unsaturated dialkyl amide.

name: Johnson-Claisen rearrangement
reagents: allylic alcohol; triethyl orthoacetate; weak acid (propionic acid)
definition: The coupling and subsequent [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of an allylic alcohol and trimethyl orthoacetate to give a gamma,delta-unsaturated alkyl ester.

name: Swern oxidation
reagents: alcohol; DMSO; oxalyl chloride; triethylamine
definition: The oxidation of a primary alcohol or secondary alcohol to an aldehyde or ketone respectively. Does not work with allylic or benzylic alcohols.

name: Finkelstein reaction
reagents: alkyl chloride/bromide; sodium iodide
definition: The conversion of an alkyl chloride, alkyl bromide or alkyl sulfonate ester to an alkyl iodide by SN2 substitution. The reaction relies upon the equilibrium being pushed to completion by the precipitation.

name: Lossen rearrangement
reagents: hydroxamic acid derivative (O-acyl); base or heat
definition: The derivatisation (for example with tosyl chloride) and subsequent rearrangement of a hydroxamic acid to give an isocyanate.

name: Nef reaction
reagents: nitroalkane; base (NaOH); strong acid (H2SO4)
definition: The conversion of a primary nitroalkane or secondary nitroalkane to an aldehyde or ketone, respectively.

name: Japp-Klingemann reaction
reagents: aryl diazonium salt; beta-keto ester or beta-keto acid; base
definition: The reaction of a doubly activated methylene compound that has at least one carbonyl substituent with an aryl azide to give a hydrazone. Usually there is concomitant cleaving and oxidation of one of the carbonyl substituents.

name: Doebner-Miller reaction
reagents: aniline; alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound; strong acid (HCl)
definition: The formation of a quinoline from a primary aromatic amine and an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

name: Fmoc protection
reagents: amine; Fmoc-Cl or Fmoc-OSu; base (NaHCO3, DIPEA)
definition: The protection of an amine (often a peptide) as its 9H-fluoren-9-ylmethoxycarbonyl derivative.

name: Paal-Knorr synthesis
reagents: 1,4-dicarbonyl compound; acid (or NH3/RNH2 for pyrroles; P4S10/Lawesson reagent for thiophenes)
definition: The cyclisation of a 1,4-dicarbonyl compound with another molecule to give a five-membered aromatic ring compound.

name: Paal-Knorr furan synthesis
reagents: 1,4-diketone; acid (H2SO4, P2O5, TsOH); dehydrating
definition: The cyclisation of a 1,4-dicarbonyl compound with an acid catalyst to give a furan.

name: Paal-Knorr thiophene synthesis
reagents: 1,4-diketone; phosphorus pentasulfide (P4S10) or Lawesson's reagent
definition: The cyclisation of a 1,4-dicarbonyl compound with phosphorus pentasulfide to give a thiophene.

name: Paal-Knorr pyrrole synthesis
reagents: 1,4-diketone; ammonia or primary amine
definition: The cyclisation of a 1,4-dicarbonyl compound with an amine to give a pyrrole.

name: Schotten-Baumann reaction
reagents: amine or alcohol; acid chloride; aqueous base (NaOH)
definition: The coupling of an alcohol or amine with an acyl chloride to give an ester or amide. A two-phase solvent system is often used, to enable the acid generated during the reaction to be neutralised by the aqueous base, while the starting materials and products remain in the organic phase.

name: Hofmann elimination
reagents: quaternary ammonium hydroxide (from amine + MeI/Ag2O); heat
definition: The elimination of a methylated amine from an alkylamine to form an olefin. The reaction proceeds via the quaternary ammonium salt.

name: Fischer-Speier esterification
reagents: carboxylic acid; alcohol (excess); strong acid catalyst (H2SO4, TsOH)
definition: The esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol. Various Lewis acids or Bronsted acids may be used as catalyst.

name: Weerman reaction
reagents: alpha-hydroxy nitrile (cyanohydrin); ammonia
definition: The degradation of an alpha-hydroxy amide or an alpha,beta-unsaturated amide to the lower homologue aldehyde, especially in carbohydrate chemistry. The process proceeds via Hofmann degradation.

name: Dakin reaction
reagents: ortho- or para-hydroxy aryl aldehyde/ketone; H2O2; base (NaOH)
definition: The reaction of ortho- or para-phenolic (or ortho- or para-anilinic) aldehydes or ketones with hydrogen peroxide to form bisphenols (or hydroxy anilines) and carboxylic acids.

name: Schmidt rearrangement, carboxylic acid
reagents: carboxylic acid; hydrazoic acid (HN3); H2SO4
definition: The reaction of a carboxylic acid with hydrazoic acid to give the lower homologue amine, with the loss of the terminal carbon atom.

name: Schmidt rearrangement, ketone
reagents: ketone; hydrazoic acid (HN3); H2SO4 or Lewis acid
definition: The reaction of a ketone with hydrazoic acid with the insertion of an NH group between the carbonyl carbon and one of the R groups to form an amide.

name: Schmidt rearrangement, tertiary alcohol
reagents: tertiary alcohol; hydrazoic acid; H2SO4
definition: The reaction of a tertiary alcohol with hydrazoic acid with rearrangement to form an imide.

name: Schmidt rearrangement, alkene
reagents: alkene; hydrazoic acid; acid
definition: The reaction of an alkene with hydrazoic acid with rearrangement to form an imide.

name: Sommelet-Hauser rearrangement
reagents: benzyl quaternary ammonium salt; strong base (NaNH2)
definition: The [2,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement of a benzyl quaternary ammonium salt to form an aniline.

name: Dakin-West reaction
reagents: alpha-amino acid; acid anhydride (Ac2O); pyridine or base
definition: The reaction of an amino acid with an acid anhydride to give an alpha-acylamido ketone. The reaction proceeds via the mixed anhydride and an oxazolone; the product is always racemic.

name: Beckmann fragmentation
reagents: oxime; strong acid or PCl5
definition: The cleavage of an oxime to the corresponding nitrile and an alkyl halide. This reaction is related to the Beckmann rearrangement, and occurs when the R group that is anti to the oxime hydroxyl is quaternary.

name: Kharasch reaction
reagents: alkene; hydrogen halide or halogenated methane (CCl4/CBrCl3); peroxide/radical initiator
definition: The transfer of a hydrogen or halogen atom from a haloalkane to an alkene, giving the chain-extended halogenated alkane.

name: Kharasch-Sosnovsky reaction
reagents: alkene (allylic C–H); tert-butyl perbenzoate/peroxyester; Cu(I) salt
definition: The allylic oxidation of an alkene with a peroxy ester or a peroxide to give the corresponding allylic alcohol derivative. The catalyst is a copper compound.

name: Elbs persulfate oxidation, phenol variant
reagents: phenol; alkaline potassium persulfate (K2S2O8); NaOH; then acid hydrolysis
definition: The oxidation of a phenol to give a (predominantly para) diphenol using potassium persulfate.

name: Elbs persulfate oxidation, tolyl variant
reagents: tolyl/methylarene; potassium persulfate
definition: The oxidation of a methyl-substituted aromatic compound to the corresponding benzaldehyde using potassium persulfate.

name: Boyland-Sims oxidation
reagents: aromatic amine/phenol; alkaline potassium persulfate (K2S2O8)
definition: The oxidation of an aromatic amine to give a (predominantly ortho) amino aryl sulfate using potassium persulfate followed by hydrolysis to yield the corresponding aminophenol.

name: Kolbe-Schmitt reaction
reagents: phenoxide (phenol + NaOH); carbon dioxide (CO2); acid workup; pressure/heat
definition: The (predominantly ortho) carboxylation of a phenoxide.

name: Perkow reaction
reagents: trialkyl phosphite; alpha-haloketone
definition: The reaction between an alpha-halocarbonyl compound and a trialkyl phosphite to give an enol phosphate.

name: Pfitzner-Moffatt oxidation
reagents: alcohol; DMSO; DCC; acid catalyst (phosphoric/pyridinium trifluoroacetate)
definition: The oxidation of a primary or secondary alcohol to the corresponding aldehyde or ketone respectively using dimethyl sulfoxide, 1,3-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide and acid. The reaction proceeds via an alkoxysulfonium ylide.

name: Willgerodt reaction
reagents: aryl alkyl ketone; sulfur; amine (morpholine); ammonium polysulfide
definition: The conversion of an aryl alkyl ketone to an amide and/or an ammonium salt of a carboxylic acid using ammonium polysulfide. The carbonyl group of the product is always at the end of the alkyl chain.

name: Willgerodt-Kindler reaction
reagents: aryl alkyl ketone; sulfur; secondary amine (morpholine)
definition: The conversion of an aryl alkyl ketone to an amide using sulfur and dry ammonia or a primary or secondary amine. The amide carbonyl group is always at the end of the alkyl chain.

name: Tishchenko reaction
reagents: aldehyde (2 equiv.); aluminium alkoxide (Al(OEt)3)
definition: The formation of an ester from two aldehydes via a disproportionation process using a metal alkoxide to oxidise one aldehyde and reduce the other.

name: Zimmermann reaction
reagents: nitroaromatic; zinc dust; NaOH (or NH4Cl)
definition: The reaction between a methylene ketone and a polynitro aromatic compound.

name: Neber rearrangement
reagents: oxime tosylate (ketoxime O-sulfonate); base (KOEt/KOH)
definition: The rearrangement of the sulfonic ester of a ketoxime in base to give an alpha-amino ketone.

name: Nozaki-Hiyama-Kishi reaction
reagents: aldehyde; vinyl/aryl halide or triflate; CrCl2; NiCl2 (catalytic)
definition: A coupling reaction of an aldehyde to an allyl, vinyl or aryl halide or triflate in the presence of chromium(II). It is catalysed by nickel.

name: Buchwald-Hartwig amination
reagents: aryl halide or triflate; amine; base (NaOtBu, Cs2CO3)
catalyst: Pd2(dba)3 or Pd(OAc)2; phosphine ligand (BINAP, XPhos); palladium atom
definition: A reaction in which an aryl halide or aryl triflate reacts with a primary or secondary amine in the presence of base to give a secondary or tertiary amine. It is catalysed by a palladium catalyst.

name: Hiyama coupling
reagents: organosilane; aryl halide; fluoride activator (TBAF) or base
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where an organosilane reacts with an organic halide or triflate. It is catalysed by a palladium or nickel complex.

name: Stevens rearrangement
reagents: quaternary ammonium salt; strong base (NaNH2, NaOH)
definition: The 1,2-rearrangement of an alpha-methylene ammonium salt or alpha-methylene sulfonium salt to an amine or sulfide in the presence of strong base.

name: Stevens rearrangement, ammonium
reagents: quaternary ammonium salt; strong base (NaNH2, NaOH)
definition: The 1,2-rearrangement of an alpha-methylene ammonium salt to an amine in the presence of strong base.

name: Stevens rearrangement, sulfonium
reagents: quaternary ammonium salt; strong base (NaNH2, NaOH)
definition: The 1,2-rearrangement of an alpha-methylene sulfonium salt to a sulfide in the presence of strong base.

name: 2-aza-Cope rearrangement
reagents: homoallylic iminium (from amine + aldehyde); acid; heat
definition: The rearrangement of a 2-aza-1,5-hexadiene to form an imine.

name: 3-aza-Cope rearrangement
reagents: N-allyl enamine; heat
definition: The rearrangement of a 3-aza-1,5-hexadiene to form a delta,epsilon-unsaturated imine.

name: 1-aza-Cope rearrangement
reagents: N-allyl imine or enamine; heat
definition: The rearrangement of a delta,epsilon-unsaturated imine to form a 3-aza-1,5-hexadiene.

name: Steglich rearrangement
reagents: O-acylated azlactone/oxazole; DMAP catalyst (4-dimethylaminopyridine)
definition: The rearrangement of an oxazolyl carbonate to a C-carboxyazlactone.

name: Strecker reaction
reagents: aldehyde/ketone; ammonia or amine; cyanide source (KCN, NaCN, TMSCN); then hydrolysis
definition: An addition reaction between a carbonyl compound, an inorganic cyanide and an ammonium salt, followed by hydrolysis, to give an alpha-amino carboxylic acid.

name: Nazarov cyclisation
reagents: divinyl ketone; Brønsted or Lewis acid (H2SO4, FeCl3, BF3)
definition: The acid-catalysed cyclisation of a divinylketone to give a cyclopentenone.

name: Fleming-Tamao oxidation
reagents: organosilane (Si–C bond); H2O2; KF/KHCO3 (or Hg(OAc)2/peracid)
definition: The stereospecific oxidation of a (phenyldimethylsilyl)alkane to the corresponding alcohol using bromine, usually generated in situ from potassium bromide and peracetic acid.

name: Tamao oxidation
reagents: alkoxy/halosilane; H2O2; KF; KHCO3
definition: The stereospecific oxidation of a (halosilyl)alkane to the corresponding alcohol using potassium fluoride and hydrogen peroxide.

name: Sakurai reaction, aldehyde or ketone
reagents: allylsilane; aldehyde/ketone; Lewis acid (TiCl4, BF3·OEt2)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction in which an aldehyde or ketone reacts with allyltrimethylsilane to form a homoallylic alcohol.

name: Sakurai reaction, enone
reagents: allylsilane; electrophile; Lewis acid
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction in which an enone reacts with allyltrimethylsilane to form a delta,epsilon-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

name: Sakurai reaction, acid chloride
reagents: allylsilane; electrophile; Lewis acid
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction in which an acid chloride reacts with allyltrimethylsilane to form a gamma,delta-unsaturated ketone.

name: Sakurai reaction, acetal or ketal
reagents: allylsilane; electrophile; Lewis acid
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction in which an acetal or ketal reacts with allyltrimethylsilane to form a homoallylic ether.

name: Sakurai reaction, epoxide
reagents: allylsilane; electrophile; Lewis acid
definition: A ring-breaking reaction in which an epoxide reacts with allyltrimethylsilane to form a hydroxy alkene.

name: Cannizzaro reaction
reagents: non-enolisable aldehyde (2 equiv.); concentrated NaOH or KOH
definition: The disproportionation of a non-enolisable aldehyde to the corresponding carboxylic acid and alcohol. The reaction is base-catalysed.

name: Pummerer rearrangement
reagents: sulfoxide; acetic anhydride (Ac2O); base or acid
definition: The conversion of a sulfoxide with an alpha-hydrogen to an alpha-substituted thioether. The reaction is usually performed with an acid anhydride or acyl halide.

name: Polonovski reaction
reagents: tertiary amine N-oxide; acetic anhydride
definition: The reaction of a tertiary amine oxide with an anhydride or acyl chloride to give an N,N-disubstituted acetamide and an aldehyde.

name: Polonovski-Potier reaction
reagents: tertiary amine N-oxide; trifluoroacetic anhydride
definition: The reaction of a tertiary amine oxide with trifluoroacetic anhydride to give an N,N-disubstituted acetamide and an aldehyde.

name: Menshutkin reaction
reagents: tertiary amine; alkyl halide
definition: The alkylation of a tertiary amine with an alkyl halide to the corresponding ammonium salt.

name: Strecker degradation
reagents: alpha-amino acid; oxidant (alloxan, dicarbonyl compound)
definition: The deamination and decarboxylation of amino acids to imines and then to aldehydes or ketones, in the presence of a carbonyl compound (especially an alpha,beta-dicarbonyl compound or a reducing sugar such as glucose). The reaction is involved in the generation of meat aromas/flavours in cooking.

name: Wohl-Ziegler bromination
reagents: allylic/benzylic substrate; N-bromosuccinimide (NBS); radical initiator (AIBN or benzoyl peroxide)
definition: The allylic or benzylic bromination of hydrocarbons using an N-bromoimide and a radical initiator, to give an allylic or benzylic bromide.

name: Wolff-Kishner reduction
reagents: ketone/aldehyde; hydrazine (N2H4); strong base (KOH, KOtBu); high-boiling solvent
definition: The reduction of an aldehyde or ketone to the corresponding methylene compound, using hydrazine hydrate and a base.

name: Wolff-Kishner reduction, Huang-Minlon modification
reagents: ketone/aldehyde; hydrazine hydrate; KOH; diethylene glycol
definition: The reduction of an aldehyde or ketone to the corresponding methylene compound, using hydrazine hydrate and a base in refluxing ethylene glycol.

name: Zemplen transesterification
reagents: ester; catalytic sodium methoxide (NaOMe); methanol
definition: The reduction of an ester to the corresponding alcohol, using sodium methoxide in dry methanol.

name: Ferrier rearrangement
reagents: glycal (acetylated); alcohol (nucleophile); Lewis acid (BF3·OEt2)
definition: The rearrangement of an O-alkenyl acetal to give the corresponding beta-alkoxy carbonyl compound.

name: Petasis reaction
reagents: amine; carbonyl (glyoxylic acid, salicylaldehyde); vinyl- or aryl-boronic acid
definition: The alkylation of an amine with a boronic acid and an aldehyde to give a substituted amine.

name: Achmatowicz rearrangement
reagents: furfuryl alcohol; oxidant (NBS, mCPBA, or singlet oxygen)
definition: A rearrangement of a furfuryl alcohol derivative to a dihydropyranone, from which monosaccharides may be synthesised.

name: Biginelli reaction
reagents: aldehyde; beta-keto ester; urea; acid catalyst (HCl, Lewis acid)
definition: A three-component coupling of a beta-keto ester, an aldehyde and urea to give a 3,4-dihydropyrimidinone.

name: Blaise reaction
reagents: nitrile; alpha-bromoester; zinc metal
definition: The coupling of an alpha-bromo ester with a nitrile to give a beta-ketoester, in the presence of zinc.

name: Bergman cyclisation
reagents: enediyne; heat (or light)
definition: The cyclisation of an ene-diyne to give a 1,4-diradical cyclohexatriene. The diradical usually aromatises.

name: Noyori asymmetric hydrogenation, alkene
reagents: alkene (enamide/allylic alcohol); H2; Ru–BINAP complex
definition: The homogeneous asymmetric catalytic hydrogenation of a C=C double bond using a ruthenium(II) BINAP catalyst.

name: Noyori asymmetric hydrogenation, carbonyl
reagents: ketone; H2 (or iPrOH); Ru–BINAP–diamine catalyst; base (KOtBu)
definition: The homogeneous asymmetric catalytic hydrogenation of a carbonyl bond using a ruthenium(II) BINAP catalyst.

name: Passerini reaction
reagents: aldehyde or ketone; carboxylic acid; isocyanide
definition: The reaction between an isonitrile, a carboxylic acid and aldehyde or ketone to give an alpha-acyloxy amide.

name: Carroll rearrangement
reagents: allylic beta-keto ester; heat (decarboxylation)
definition: An adaptation of the Claisen rearrangement that transforms a beta-keto allyl ester into a gamma,delta-allyl ketone. It uses base and high temperature or milder conditions with a ruthenium or palladium complex as catalyst.

name: Bose-Mitsunobu reaction
reagents: alcohol; PPh3; DEAD/DIAD; carboxylic acid (e.g. 4-nitrobenzoic acid)
definition: A Mitsunobu reaction, where an alcohol is converted to something else with inversion at the stereocentre, using diphenylphosphoryl azide.

name: Stork-Wittig olefination
reagents: alpha-silyl or stabilized phosphonium ylide with alkoxy/aryl; aldehyde; strong base
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where an aldehyde reacts with a phosphonium salt to give a Z-iodoalkene. The reaction is mediated by sodium or potassium hexamethyldisilazide.

name: Cadogan carbazole synthesis
reagents: 2-nitrobiphenyl; triethyl phosphite (P(OEt)3) or PPh3; heat
definition: The reduction of a 2-nitrobiaryl compound to give a carbazole.

name: Cadogan coupling
reagents: nitroarene/nitroso compound; triethyl phosphite or PPh3
definition: The arylation of an arylamine mediated by isopentyl nitrite.

name: Zweifel diene synthesis
reagents: vinylboronate (alkenylboronic ester); alkenyl halide; iodine; NaOMe
definition: The carbon-carbon homocoupling reaction of a pair of alkyne molecules using a borane and iodine. The reaction proceeds via a borane intermediate.

name: Dess-Martin oxidation
reagents: alcohol; Dess-Martin periodinane (DMP)
definition: The oxidation of a primary alcohol to an aldehyde or a secondary alcohol to a ketone using the Dess-Martin periodinane.

name: Criegee oxidation
reagents: sulfide or sulfoxide; peroxy acid (mCPBA)
definition: The oxidative cleavage of an alpha,beta-diol using lead tetraacetate to give the corresponding carbonyl compounds.

name: Simmons-Smith reaction
reagents: alkene; diiodomethane (CH2I2); zinc-copper couple
definition: A ring formation reaction where an alkene reacts with a dihalomethane in the presence of a metal atom or metal complexes to form a cyclopropane. The traditional reaction uses a zinc-copper couple and diiodomethane.

name: Wittig rearrangement
reagents: ether; strong base (alkyllithium)
definition: Any of a family of sigmatropic rearrangements that involve the migration of a group on an electronegative atom (O or N) to a carbon atom.

name: [1,2]-Wittig rearrangement
reagents: ether (benzyl/allyl); strong base (n-BuLi)
definition: A base-mediated 1,2-sigmatropic rearrangement of an ether to give an alcohol.

name: [2,3]-Wittig rearrangement
reagents: allyl ether; strong base (n-BuLi, KH)
definition: A base-mediated 2,3-sigmatropic rearrangement of an allyl ether to give a homoallylic alcohol.

name: [1,2]-aza-Wittig rearrangement
reagents: ether; strong base (alkyllithium)
definition: A base-mediated 1,2-sigmatropic rearrangement of a tertiary amine to give a secondary amine.

name: [2,3]-aza-Wittig rearrangement
reagents: ether; strong base (alkyllithium)
definition: A base-mediated 2,3-sigmatropic rearrangement of an activated tertiary allyl amine, to give a secondary homoallylic amine.

name: Fenton reaction
reagents: hydrogen peroxide (H2O2); iron(II) salt (Fe2+)
definition: An oxidation reaction involving Fenton's reagent.

name: Hantzsch pyridine synthesis
reagents: aldehyde; 2 equiv. beta-keto ester; ammonia (or NH4OAc); then oxidant (HNO3, DDQ)
definition: A ring-forming reaction between two equivalents of a beta-ketoester, an aldehyde and ammonia (or an ammonium salt), to give a dihydropyridine. The dihydropyridine can be oxidised to a pyridine using an oxidising agent.

name: Fischer-Tropsch process
reagents: carbon monoxide; hydrogen (syngas); heterogeneous Fe or Co catalyst
definition: A process in which carbon monoxide and hydrogen ('syngas') are converted into various liquid hydrocarbons.

name: Stork-Crabtree hydrogenation
reagents: alkene; hydrogen (H2); Crabtree's catalyst ([Ir(cod)(PCy3)(py)]PF6)
definition: A hydrogenation in which a metal-ligating group distant from the reacting alkene directs the attack of hydrogen, giving preferentially one stereoisomer of the product.

name: Aufbau reaction
reagents: ethylene; triethylaluminium (AlEt3)
definition: The insertion of alkenes (usually ethene) into the Al-C bond of an aluminium alkyl, to give a long-chain aluminium alkyl that can go on to react again, or can decompose into the corresponding terminal alkene. The addition of transition metals results in reliable production of high molecular weight polymers.

name: Luche reaction
reagents: ketone/enone; NaBH4; CeCl3 (cerium(III) chloride)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where an aldehyde or ketone reacts with an allyl halide and zinc to give a homoallylic alcohol.

name: Luche reduction
reagents: enone; NaBH4; CeCl3·7H2O (Luche conditions)
definition: The chemoselective reduction of an enone to give an allylic alcohol, using sodium borohydride and an lanthanoid chloride, typically cerium chloride.

name: Lindgren oxidation
reagents: aldehyde; sodium chlorite (NaClO2); scavenger (2-methyl-2-butene); buffer (NaH2PO4)
definition: The oxidation of an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid with chlorite.

name: Rosenmund-von Braun reaction
reagents: aryl halide; copper(I) cyanide (CuCN)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where an aryl halide reacts with copper(I) cyanide to give an aryl nitrile.

name: Woehler reaction
reagents: ammonium cyanate (NH4OCN)
definition: The formation of urea from ammonium cyanate. Ammonium cyanate is unstable, and so is formed in situ from either (a) cyanic acid and ammonia, (b) a metal cyanate and an ammonium salt, or (c) a metal cyanate and ammonia.

name: Fetizon oxidation
reagents: alcohol; silver carbonate on Celite (Fetizon's reagent; Ag2CO3)
definition: The oxidation of a primary alcohol to an aldehyde or a secondary alcohol to a ketone using Fetizon's reagent.

name: Vorbrueggen condensation
reagents: silylated nucleobase; protected sugar acetate; Lewis acid (TMSOTf, SnCl4)
definition: The substitution of an acylated sugar with a silylated base to give a nucleoside.

name: Julia-Kocienski olefination
reagents: alkyl heteroaryl sulfone (e.g. PT-sulfone); strong base (KHMDS); aldehyde
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between a tetrazole sulfone and an aldehyde or ketone to give a (typically trans) alkene.

name: Mori-Ban indole synthesis
reagents: aromatic nitro compound; alkyl vinyl ether/ketone; base
definition: An intramolecular Heck reaction of an ortho-halo-aniline with an alkene, catalysed by palladium.

name: Yamaguchi lactonisation
reagents: carboxylic acid; 2,4,6-trichlorobenzoyl chloride (Yamaguchi reagent); Et3N; DMAP; alcohol
definition: The intramolecular esterification of a carboxylic acid group with an alcohol group using 2,4,6-trichlorobenzoyl chloride (Yamaguchi reagent) - an intramolecular Yamaguchi esterification.

name: Yamaguchi esterification
reagents: carboxylic acid; 2,4,6-trichlorobenzoyl chloride (Yamaguchi reagent); Et3N; DMAP; alcohol
definition: The esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol using 2,4,6-trichlorobenzoyl chloride (Yamaguchi reagent).

name: Tsuji-Trost reaction
reagents: allylic acetate/carbonate; soft nucleophile (malonate, amine); base
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction in which a nucleophile reacts with an allyl acetate, allyl halide, allyl carbonate, allyl carbamate, allyl phosphate, allyl sulfone or allyl nitro compound to give an allyl compound. The reaction is catalsed by Pd(0).

name: Clauson-Kaas reaction
reagents: primary amine; 2,5-dimethoxytetrahydrofuran; acetic acid
definition: A ring rearrangement reaction where an amine reacts with a 2,5-dialkoxytetrahydrofuran to give a pyrrole.

name: Boc deprotection
reagents: Boc-protected amine; strong acid (TFA or HCl in dioxane)
definition: An amino group deprotection reaction where a tertbutoxycarbonyl group is removed in acid conditions.

name: Sandmeyer halogenation
reagents: aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+, from NaNO2/HX); CuCl, CuBr or CuCN
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(I) halide to form an aromatic halide.

name: Sandmeyer pseudohalogenation
reagents: aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+, from NaNO2/HX); CuCl, CuBr or CuCN
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(II) pseudohalide to form an aromatic pseudohalide.

name: Jones oxidation
reagents: alcohol; chromic acid (CrO3/H2SO4/H2O = Jones reagent); acetone
definition: An oxidation reaction where an alcohol is oxidized to the corresponding carbonyl compound by a dichromate ion.

name: Pinner reaction
reagents: nitrile; alcohol; anhydrous HCl (gas)
definition: A functional group modification where a nitrile reacts with an alcohol under acid catalysis to form an amidine or ester.

name: Friedel-Crafts reaction
reagents: arene; alkyl/acyl halide; Lewis acid (AlCl3)
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction between an arene and a carbonyl compound (an acylation) or an alkyl compound that can form a carbocation (an alkylation) to form a substituted arene.

name: Demko-Sharpless reaction
reagents: nitrile; sodium azide (NaN3); zinc salt (ZnBr2)
definition: A functional group modification of a nitrile to a 1H-tetrazole by addition of sodium azide.

name: Griess reaction
reagents: aromatic amine; nitrous acid (NaNO2/HCl); coupling partner (phenol or aniline)
definition: A diazotisation that proceeds by the addition of nitrous acid, nitric acid and water, resulting in a diazonium nitrate salt.

name: Chan-Lam coupling
reagents: arylboronic acid; amine or alcohol; Cu(OAc)2; base (pyridine, Et3N); O2 (air)
definition: Arylation of an amine or an alcohol with an arylboronic acid, stannane or siloxane in air with a copper acetate catalyst.

name: Eschweiler-Clarke methylation
reagents: primary/secondary amine; formaldehyde (HCHO); formic acid (HCOOH)
definition: N-methylation of a primary or secondary amine with formic acid and formaldehyde to yield a tertiary amine.

name: Scholl reaction
reagents: two arene rings; Lewis acid (AlCl3); acid
definition: Coupling of two aromatic rings in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst.

name: Robinson annulation
reagents: ketone; methyl vinyl ketone (MVK) or equivalent; base (NaOEt, KOH)
definition: Reaction of a cyclohexanone with methyl vinyl ketone to form a fused-ring cyclohexenone. It is a Michael reaction followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation.

name: Tiffeneau-Demjanov rearrangement
reagents: beta-amino alcohol/cyclic ketone; nitrous acid (NaNO2/HCl) or diazomethane
definition: Rearrangement of a beta-amino alcohol to yield a carbonyl compound. In the first step the amine is diazotised by reaction with nitrous acid.

name: Demjanov rearrangement
reagents: primary aliphatic amine; nitrous acid (NaNO2/HCl)
definition: Substitution reaction of a primary amine via deazotisation to yield a mixture of the corresponding primary alcohol and secondary alcohol.

name: Favorskii rearrangement
reagents: alpha-halo ketone (enolisable); base (alkoxide, hydroxide)
definition: Base-catalysed rearrangement of an alpha-haloketone to a carboxylic acid or ester or amide.

name: Wallach degradation
reagents: azoxybenzene; concentrated sulfuric acid
definition: Favorskii rearrangement of a cyclic alpha-dibromoketone followed by decarboxylation to yield a ring-contracted cyclic ketone.

name: Seyferth-Gilbert homologation
reagents: aldehyde or ketone; dimethyl (diazomethyl)phosphonate anion; base (KOtBu)
definition: Reaction of a carbonyl compound with a dimethyl diazomethyl phosphonate under basic conditions to yield an alkyne.

name: Seyferth-Gilbert aldehyde homologation
reagents: aldehyde or ketone; dimethyl (diazomethyl)phosphonate anion; base (KOtBu)
definition: Reaction of an aldehyde with a dimethyl diazomethyl phosphonate under basic conditions to yield a terminal alkyne.

name: Seyferth-Gilbert ketone homologation
reagents: aldehyde or ketone; dimethyl (diazomethyl)phosphonate anion; base (KOtBu)
definition: Reaction of a ketone with a dimethyl diazomethyl phosphonate under basic conditions to yield a terminal alkyne.

name: Seyferth-Gilbert-Bestmann homologation
reagents: aldehyde; Ohira-Bestmann reagent (dimethyl 1-diazo-2-oxopropylphosphonate); K2CO3; MeOH
definition: Seyferth-Gilbert aldehyde homologation where the Seyferth-Gilbert reagent is generated in situ by reaction with methanol and potassium carbonate.

name: Knorr pyrazole synthesis
reagents: hydrazine; 1,3-diketone or beta-keto ester
definition: Synthesis of a pyrazole by condensation of a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound with a hydrazine, hydrazide, semicarbazide or aminoguanidine.

name: Knorr quinoline synthesis
reagents: beta-keto anilide; concentrated H2SO4 or PPA
definition: Synthesis of an alpha-hydroxyquinoline by reaction of a beta-ketoester and an arylamine then dehydration with concentrated sulfuric acid.

name: Larock indole synthesis
reagents: o-haloaniline; internal alkyne; base (K2CO3, LiCl)
definition: Palladium-catalysed synthesis of a 2,3-substituted indole by reaction of an ortho-iodoaniline with an internal alkyne.

name: Phillips benzimidazole synthesis
reagents: o-phenylenediamine; carboxylic acid; mineral acid (HCl); heat
definition: Reaction of an ortho-diaminobenzene with a carboxylic acid under heat to yield a benzimidazole.

name: Pinner pyrimidine synthesis
reagents: amidine; 1,3-dicarbonyl compound; acid or base
definition: Reaction of a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound with an amidine to yield a pyrimidine.

name: Prilezhaev epoxidation
reagents: alkene; peracid (mCPBA, peracetic acid)
definition: Epoxidation of an alkene by reaction with a peroxy acid.

name: Appel halogenation
reagents: alcohol; triphenylphosphine (PPh3); carbon tetrahalide (CCl4, CBr4) or halogen source
definition: Conversion of an alcohol to an alkyl halide with triphenylphosphine and a halide source.

name: Appel iodination
reagents: alcohol; PPh3; I2; imidazole
definition: Conversion of an alcohol to an alkyl iodide with triphenylphosphine and tetraiodomethane.

name: Appel chlorination
reagents: alcohol; PPh3; CCl4 (or hexachloroacetone)
definition: Conversion of an alcohol to an alkyl chloride with triphenylphosphine and tetrachloromethane.

name: Appel bromination
reagents: alcohol; PPh3; CBr4 (or Br2)
definition: Conversion of an alcohol to an alkyl bromide with triphenylphosphine and tetrabromomethane or bromine.

name: Hofmann rearrangement
reagents: primary amide; halogen (Br2) or hypohalite (NaOBr); NaOH
definition: Rearrangement of a primary carboxylic amide to an isocyanate.

name: Hofmann reaction
reagents: primary amide; NaOBr (Br2/NaOH)
definition: Conversion of a primary carboxylic amide to the lower homologue primary amine. The first step is the Hofmann rearrangement

name: Newman-Kwart rearrangement
reagents: O-aryl thiocarbamate; heat (200–300 °C)
definition: Rearrangement of an O-aryl thiocarbamate to an S-aryl thiocarbamate by migration of the aryl group.

name: Kröhnke pyridine synthesis
reagents: alpha-pyridinium methyl ketone; alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl; ammonium acetate
definition: Condensation of a 1,5-diketone with ammonium acetate in acetic acid to form a pyridine.

name: Gattermann chlorination
reagents: arene diazonium salt; copper powder; HCl
definition: A Gattermann halogenation where the aryl diazonium salt reacts with copper powder and hydrochloric acid to yield an aromatic chloride.

name: Gattermann bromination
reagents: arene diazonium salt; copper powder; HBr
definition: A Gattermann halogenation where the aryl diazonium salt reacts with copper powder and hydrobromic acid to yield an aromatic bromide.

name: Sakurai reaction
reagents: allylsilane; electrophile; Lewis acid
definition: Reaction of allyltrimethylsilane with a carbon electrophile to allylate the carbon electrophile.

name: Fries rearrangement
reagents: aryl ester (phenolic); Lewis acid (AlCl3) or hv
definition: Rearrangement of the acyl group in a phenolate ester to the ortho- and/or para-position. It is catalysed by a Lewis acid.

name: Duff reaction
reagents: phenol; hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA); acid (glycerol/boric acid or TFA)
definition: Formylation of a phenol or aromatic amine with hexamethylenetetramine in acidic conditions.

name: Pauson-Khand reaction
reagents: alkyne; alkene; carbon monoxide (CO); Co2(CO)8
definition: A [2+2+1] cycloaddition between an alkyne, an alkene and carbon monoxide to form an alpha-beta-unsaturated cyclopentenone.

name: Algar-Flynn-Oyamada reaction
reagents: 2'-hydroxychalcone; alkaline hydrogen peroxide (H2O2/NaOH)
definition: A fused-ring-system formation reaction where a flavonol is produced by oxidation of a chalcone with alkaline hydrogen peroxide.

name: Allan-Robinson flavone synthesis
reagents: o-hydroxyaryl ketone; aromatic anhydride; sodium salt of the aromatic acid
definition: Reaction of ortho-hydroxyaryl ketones with aromatic carboxylic acid anhydrides to yield a flavone.

name: Allan-Robinson isoflavone synthesis
reagents: o-hydroxyaryl ketone; aromatic anhydride; sodium salt of aromatic acid
definition: Reaction of ortho-hydroxyaryl ketones with aromatic carboxylic acid anhydrides to yield an isoflavone.

name: Amadori rearrangement
reagents: N-glycoside of aldose; acid catalyst
definition: Rearrangement of an aldose N-glycoside to a ketose N-glycoside by acid or base catalysis.

name: Allan-Robinson reaction
reagents: o-hydroxyaryl ketone; aromatic anhydride; sodium salt of aromatic acid
definition: Reaction of ortho-hydroxyaryl ketones with aromatic acid anhydrides to yield a flavone or isoflavone.

name: Meyer-Schuster rearrangement
reagents: propargylic alcohol; acid catalyst (H+, Lewis acid)
definition: Rearrangement of a propargyl alcohol to an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound via an allene intermediate to yield the gamma-substituted product.

name: Rupe rearrangement
reagents: tertiary propargylic alcohol; acid catalyst
definition: Rearrangement of a propargyl alcohol to an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound via an enyne intermediate to yield the beta-substituted product.

name: Still-Gennari modification
reagents: bis(trifluoroethyl)phosphonate; strong base (KHMDS, 18-crown-6); aldehyde
definition: A Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons reaction that uses phosphonates with electron-withdrawing groups and dissociating conditions to produce predominantly Z-olefins.

name: Tebbe olefination
reagents: ester or ketone; Tebbe reagent (Cp2Ti(μ-Cl)(μ-CH2)AlMe2); pyridine base
definition: Reaction of an aldehyde or ketone or carboxylic ester or amide with the Tebbe reagent to yield an olefin or an enol ether or an enamine.

name: Myers-Saito cyclisation
reagents: enyne-allene; heat
definition: Cyclization of a enynyl allene to yield a toluene biradical with radical centres on the methyl group and at the meta position.

name: Bamberger rearrangement
reagents: N-phenylhydroxylamine; aqueous strong acid (H2SO4)
definition: Rearrangement of an N-phenylhydroxamine in acid to yield a para-aminophenol.

name: Bartoli indole synthesis
reagents: ortho-substituted nitroarene; vinyl Grignard reagent (3 equiv.)
definition: Reaction of an ortho-substituted nitroarene with a vinyl Grignard reagent to yield a 7-substituted indole.

name: Barton-Zard reaction
reagents: nitroalkene; alpha-isocyanoacetate; base (DBU, tBuOK)
definition: Reaction of a nitroalkene with an alpha-isocyanoacetate to yield a substituted pyrrole.

name: Béchamp reduction
reagents: nitroarene; iron metal; acid (HCl or AcOH)
definition: Reduction of an aromatic nitro compound to the corresponding arene by iron in some form in aqueous acid.

name: Beirut reaction
reagents: benzofuroxan; enamine, enolate or 1,3-dicarbonyl
definition: Reaction of a benzofurazan 1-oxide with an enamine or enolate to yield a quinoxaline-1,4-dioxide.

name: Bénary reaction
reagents: alpha-halo ketone; beta-ketoester; pyridine or base
definition: Reaction of a beta-aminovinylketone with a Grignard reagent to yield a substituted alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl compound.

name: Feist-Bénary synthesis
reagents: alpha-haloketone; beta-dicarbonyl compound; pyridine/amine base
definition: Reaction of an alpha-haloketone or alpha-haloether with a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound in the presence of pyridine to yield a substituted furan.

name: Nef synthesis
reagents: nitroalkane (nitronate salt); acid (H2SO4)
definition: Reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with a sodium acetylide to yield a propargyl alcohol.

name: Krapcho decarboxylation
reagents: alkyl malonate/beta-keto ester; halide salt (LiCl, NaCl); DMSO; water; heat
definition: Reaction of an ester with an electron-withdrawing group alpha- to the ester functionality with a metal halide or pseudohalide to yield the shorter homologous system.

name: Cadogan cyclization
reagents: o-nitrobiaryl or nitrostyrene; triethyl phosphite (P(OEt)3) or PPh3
definition: Reaction of an aromatic nitro compound with an unsaturated substituent at the alpha-position to form a fused-ring nitrogen heterocycle.

name: Cadogan indole synthesis
reagents: o-nitrobiaryl or nitrostyrene; triethyl phosphite (P(OEt)3) or PPh3
definition: A Cadogan cyclization that results in an indole.

name: Benkeser reduction
reagents: arene; Li or Na metal; NH3/amine; alcohol
definition: Addition of hydrogen atoms to unsaturated rings by means of alkali metals in low-molecular weight amines.

name: Madelung indole synthesis
reagents: N-acyl-o-toluidine; strong base (NaOEt, KOtBu, BuLi); heat
definition: Reaction of an N-(2-alkylphenyl)alkanamide with strong base to form an indole.

name: Mumm rearrangement
reagents: imidate (isoimide); heat
definition: Rearrangement of an acyl imidate to form a carboximide.

name: Chapman rearrangement
reagents: aryl imidate; heat (250–300 °C)
definition: Rearrangement of an aryl imino ether to yield an N,N-diaryl amide.

name: Bergmann azlactone peptide synthesis
reagents: N-acylglycine; aromatic aldehyde; acetic anhydride; sodium acetate
definition: Reaction of an acetylated amino acid with an aldehyde then with a second amino acid, then hydrogenation and hydrolysis to form a dipeptide. It proceeds via an azlactone intermediate.

name: Bergmann degradation
reagents: acyl amino acid; acyl chloride; aqueous alkali
definition: Removal of a terminal amino acid residue from a peptide by benzoylation, azidation, treatment with benzyl alcohol, hydrogenation and hydrolysis.

name: Bernthsen acridine synthesis
reagents: diarylamine; carboxylic acid; ZnCl2 (Lewis acid); heat
definition: Reaction of a diarylamine in an organic acid or anhydride in the presence of zinc chloride to yield a 9-substituted acridine.

name: Betti reaction
reagents: aldehyde; 2-naphthol; ammonia or amine
definition: Reaction of a phenol, an aromatic aldehyde and a primary aromatic or heterocyclic amine to yield a Betti's base, also known as an alpha-aminobenzylphenol.

name: Bischler-Möhlau indole synthesis
reagents: alpha-bromoketone; excess aniline; heat
definition: Reaction of a terminal hydroxyketone or terminal halogenoketone with an aromatic amine to yield a 2-substituted indole.

name: Camps quinoline synthesis
reagents: o-acylaminoacetophenone; hydroxide base (NaOH)
definition: Cyclisation of an o-acylaminoacetophenone in alcoholic sodium hydroxide to form a substituted hydroxyquinoline.

name: Castro-Stephens coupling
reagents: terminal alkyne (copper acetylide); aryl halide; pyridine
definition: Palladium-catalysed coupling of copper(I) acetylides with aryl halides to yield arylacetylenes.

name: Chichibabin pyridine synthesis
reagents: aldehyde/ketone (2–3 equiv.); ammonia; catalyst (Al2O3, SiO2)
definition: Reaction of carbonyl compounds with ammonia or an amine to yield a pyridine.

name: Chichibabin reaction
reagents: pyridine or azine; sodium amide (NaNH2); liquid NH3 or PhNMe2
definition: Reaction of an azacycle with an alkali-metal amide to yield an aminated azacycle.

name: Bodroux reaction
reagents: Grignard reagent; trialkyl orthoformate or acid derivative
definition: Reaction of a carboxylic ester with a magnesium iodide alkylamide to yield a carboxamide.

name: Borsche-Drechsel cyclisation
reagents: arylhydrazone of cyclohexanone; acid (HCl, H2SO4)
definition: Rearrangement of a cyclohexanone phenylhydrazone followed by oxidation to yield a carbazole.

name: Bouveault aldehyde synthesis
reagents: Grignard reagent; N,N-disubstituted formamide (DMF); aqueous acid
definition: Reaction of an organomagnesium or organolithium compound with an N,N'-disubstituted formamide to yield the next homologous aldehyde.

name: Parham cyclisation
reagents: o-halogenated aromatic; organolithium (BuLi); electrophile
definition: Reaction of a bromoarene that has an electrophilic group at the para-position with lithium bromide or lithium iodide followed by intramolecular cyclisation to yield a fused-ring system.

name: Quelet reaction
reagents: arene; formaldehyde; HCl; ZnCl2
definition: Reaction of an aliphatic aldehyde with a phenolic ether and hydrochloric acid to yield an alpha-chloroalkylphenolic ether.

name: Chugaev reaction
reagents: xanthate ester (alcohol + CS2/NaOH/MeI); heat (150–200 °C)
definition: Elimination of a water molecule from a secondary alcohol to yield an olefin.

name: Cope elimination
reagents: tertiary amine N-oxide (amine + H2O2 or mCPBA); heat
definition: Elimination of a hydroxylamine from an amine oxide by pyrolysis to yield an olefin.

name: Sugasawa reaction
reagents: phenol; nitrile or amide; Lewis acid (BCl3, AlCl3)
definition: Reaction of an aniline with a nitrile in the presence of boron trichloride and a Lewis acid to yield an ortho-acylated aniline.

name: Saegusa oxidation
reagents: silyl enol ether; Pd(OAc)2 (stoichiometric or catalytic with benzoquinone/O2)
definition: Reaction of silyl enol ethers with palladium acetate in acetonitrile to yield an alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone.

name: Sandmeyer diphenylurea isatin synthesis
reagents: aniline; chloral hydrate; hydroxylamine hydrochloride; Na2SO4; then conc. H2SO4
definition: Reaction of diphenylthiourea with lead carbonate and potassium cyanide to form a cyanoformidine followed by ring closure and acid hydrolysis to yield isatin.

name: Sandmeyer isonitrosoacetanilide isatin synthesis
reagents: aniline; chloral hydrate; hydroxylamine hydrochloride; Na2SO4; then conc. H2SO4
definition: Reaction of aniline, hydroxylamine and chloral hydrate to form an aniline intermediate followed by cyclization in acid and hydrolysis to yield isatin.

name: Sarett oxidation
reagents: alcohol; chromium trioxide-pyridine complex (Sarett reagent; CrO3·2py)
definition: Oxidation of an alcohol with a pyridine-chromium trioxide complex to yield a carbonyl compound.

name: Sarett primary alcohol oxidation
reagents: alcohol; chromium trioxide-pyridine complex (Sarett reagent; CrO3·2py)
definition: Oxidation of a primary alcohol with a pyridine-chromium trioxide complex to yield an aldehyde.

name: Sarett secondary alcohol oxidation
reagents: alcohol; chromium trioxide-pyridine complex (Sarett reagent; CrO3·2py)
definition: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol with a pyridine-chromium trioxide complex to yield a ketone.

name: Collins oxidation
reagents: alcohol; CrO3·2 pyridine (Collins reagent)
definition: Oxidation of a primary alcohol with a pyridine-chromium trioxide complex in dichloromethane to yield an aldehyde.

name: Leuckart aldehyde reaction
reagents: aldehyde/ketone; ammonium formate or formamide
definition: Reductive amination of an aldehyde with ammonium formate or formamide to form an amine.

name: Leuckart ketone reaction
reagents: aldehyde/ketone; ammonium formate or formamide
definition: Reductive amination of a ketone with ammonium formate or formamide to form an amine.

name: Appel bromination with tetrabromomethane
reagents: alcohol; PPh3; tetrabromomethane (CBr4)
definition: Conversion of an alcohol to an alkyl bromide with triphenylphosphine and tetrabromomethane.

name: Appel bromination with bromine
reagents: alcohol; PPh3; bromine (Br2)
definition: Conversion of an alcohol to an alkyl bromide with triphenylphosphine and bromine.

name: Corey-Fuchs terminal dibromoolefination
reagents: aldehyde; CBr4; PPh3 (2 equiv.); (no BuLi at dibromoolefin stage)
definition: Reaction of an aldehyde with tetrabromomethane and triphenylphosphine to yield a terminal dibromoolefin.

name: Dess-Martin aldehyde oxidation
reagents: alcohol; Dess-Martin periodinane (DMP)
definition: A Dess-Martin oxidation of a primary alcohol to an aldehyde.

name: Dess-Martin ketone oxidation
reagents: alcohol; Dess-Martin periodinane (DMP)
definition: A Dess-Martin oxidation of a secondary alcohol to a ketone.

name: Friedlander quinoline synthesis
reagents: 2-aminobenzaldehyde or 2-aminoaryl ketone; ketone/aldehyde with alpha-CH2; acid or base
definition: Synthesis of a quinoline by reaction of a 2-aminobenzaldehyde with a ketone.

name: Gewald reaction
reagents: ketone/aldehyde; alpha-cyanoester or malononitrile; elemental sulfur (S8); amine base (morpholine)
definition: Reaction of an aldehyde or ketone with an alpha-cyanoester to form a 2-aminothiophene.

name: Niementowski quinazoline synthesis
reagents: anthranilic acid; amide; heat
definition: An azacycle synthesis where the product is a 4-oxo-3,4-dihydroquinazoline and the reactants are a 2-aminobenzoic acid and an amide.

name: Pomeranz–Fritsch reaction
reagents: benzaldehyde; aminoacetaldehyde diethyl acetal; strong acid (H2SO4)
definition: An azacycle synthesis where the product is an isoquinoline and the reactants are a benzaldehyde and a 2,2-dialkoxyethylamine.

name: Steglich esterification
reagents: carboxylic acid; alcohol; DCC (or EDC); DMAP (catalytic)
definition: An O-acylation to ester where dicyclohexylcarbodiimide is used as a coupling reagent and 4-dimethylaminopyridine as a catalyst.

name: Wenker synthesis
reagents: beta-amino alcohol; H2SO4; NaOH (2 steps)
definition: Synthesis of an aziridine by dehydrating a beta aminoalcohol with sulfuric acid.

name: Hinsberg thiophene synthesis
reagents: diethyl thiodiglycolate; 1,2-dicarbonyl compound (oxalate); base (NaOEt)
definition: Reaction of an alpha-diketone with a dialkyl thiodiacetate to form a thiophene dicarboxylic acid.

name: Suzuki-type coupling
reagents: organoboron; organic halide; base
definition: The coupling of a boronic acid or boronic ester with an unsaturated halide, triflate or sulfonate.

name: Ciamician-Dennstedt rearrangement
reagents: pyrrole or indole; dihalocarbene (CHCl3/NaOH)
definition: Expansion of a pyrrole ring by heating with a halogeno compond to form a 3-halogenopyridine.

name: Claisen-Schmidt condensation
reagents: aromatic aldehyde (no alpha-H); ketone or aldehyde with alpha-H; base (NaOH, KOH)
definition: Condensation of an aromatic aldehyde with an aliphatic aldehyde or ketone in the presence of a relatively strong base to from an alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde or ketone.

name: Corey-Bakshi-Shibata reduction
reagents: prochiral ketone; borane (BH3·THF or BH3·SMe2); CBS catalyst (chiral oxazaborolidine)
definition: Enantioselective reduction of a ketone to an alcohol with a chiral oxazaborolidine.

name: Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky reaction
reagents: sulfur ylide (dimethylsulfonium methylide from Me3S+I- and NaH; or dimethylsulfoxonium methylide); aldehyde/ketone/enone
definition: Reaction of a sulfur ylide with a double-bond to produce a three-membered ring.

name: Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky epoxide synthesis
reagents: aldehyde/ketone; sulfur ylide (trimethylsulfonium iodide + NaH or KOtBu)
definition: Reaction of a sulfur ylide with a ketone to produce an epoxide.

name: Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky cyclopropane synthesis
reagents: sulfur ylide (dimethylsulfonium methylide from Me3S+I- and NaH; or dimethylsulfoxonium methylide); aldehyde/ketone/enone
definition: Reaction of a sulfur ylide with an olefin to produce a cyclopropane.

name: Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky aziridine synthesis
reagents: imine; sulfur ylide (trimethylsulfonium iodide + strong base)
definition: Reaction of a sulfur ylide with an imine to produce an aziridine.

name: Johnson-Corey-Chaykovsky thiirane synthesis
reagents: thioketone/thioaldehyde; sulfur ylide
definition: Reaction of a sulfur ylide with a thione to produce a thiirane.

name: Liebeskind-Srogl coupling
reagents: thioester (or thioether); boronic acid; Cu(I) carboxylate (CuTC)
catalyst: Pd(0); Cu(I) thiophene-2-carboxylate; transition element atom
definition: A cross-coupling reaction where a thioester and a boronic acid react to form a ketone. It uses a metal catalyst.

name: Fukuyama coupling
reagents: thioester; organozinc reagent
definition: A cross-coupling reaction where a thioester and an organozinc halide react to form a ketone. It uses a palladium catalyst.

name: Sandmeyer fluorination
reagents: aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+, from NaNO2/HX); CuCl, CuBr or CuCN
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(I) fluoride to form an aromatic fluoride.

name: Sandmeyer chlorination
reagents: aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+, from NaNO2/HX); CuCl, CuBr or CuCN
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(I) chloride to form an aromatic chloride.

name: Sandmeyer bromination
reagents: aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+, from NaNO2/HX); CuCl, CuBr or CuCN
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(I) bromide to form an aromatic bromide.

name: Sandmeyer iodination
reagents: aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+, from NaNO2/HX); CuCl, CuBr or CuCN
definition: An aromatic substitution reaction where an aryl diazonium salt reacts with a copper(I) iodide to form an aromatic iodide.

name: Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag reaction
reagents: N-haloamine; strong acid (H2SO4); heat or hv
definition: An azacycle synthesis in which pyrrolidines or piperidines are formed by decomposition of protonated N-haloamines.

name: Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag piperidine synthesis
reagents: amine (N-chloroamine); H2SO4; hv or heat
definition: A Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag reaction in which the product is a piperidine.

name: Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag pyrrolidine synthesis
reagents: amine (N-chloroamine); H2SO4; hv or heat
definition: A Hofmann-Löffler-Freytag reaction in which the product is a pyrrolidine.

name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction
reagents: carboxylic acid; Br2; PBr3 (or red P); water
definition: An alpha-halogenation reaction where a carboxylic acid reacts with dibromine to form an alpha-bromocarboxylic acid.

name: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction of an aldehyde
reagents: aldehyde; isopropanol; Al(OiPr)3
definition: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction of an aldehyde to the corresponding primary alcohol.

name: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction of a ketone
reagents: ketone; isopropanol; Al(OiPr)3
definition: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction of a ketone to the corresponding secondary alcohol.

name: Heck-type reaction
reagents: organic halide; alkene; base
definition: A carbon-carbon coupling reaction where an organohalide or triflate couples to a terminal olefin to produce an internal olefin.

name: Conrad-Limpach cyclisation
reagents: aniline; beta-keto ester; heat (250 °C)
